summary: The note describes Meadowview's "Preventative Health: Screenings and Check-Ups for Lifelong Wellness" workshop series, starting October 10th, 2023 at the Meadowview Community Center, and uses it as a model for organizing community wellness workshops. It explains why prevention matters, then walks through planning, promoting, conducting and evaluating a workshop. A spring follow-up series is already planned based on feedback from the fall series.
one_line: Meadowview's October 2023 preventative health workshop series serves as a practical guide to planning, promoting, running and evaluating community wellness workshops.
key_facts: The Meadowview Community Center hosts the "Preventative Health: Screenings and Check-Ups for Lifelong Wellness" workshop series starting October 10th, 2023.
The series is led by local healthcare professionals and advocates such as Dr. Susan O'Malley and community organizer James Peterson.
The workshops aim to educate citizens on regular health screenings and medical check-ups to prevent diseases before they become serious.
The World Health Organization identifies prevention as a key factor in promoting health and well-being.
Meadowview's workshop series takes a universal approach, open to everyone rather than a specific age group.
Speakers include General Practitioner Dr. Susan O'Malley and local nutritionist Michael Thompson, covering topics from cancer screenings to nutritional advice for disease prevention.
A typical Meadowview day has a keynote speech from a local health leader, breakout sessions on different health screenings, and an interactive workshop on self-examinations.
Meadowview promoted the October series through local radio spots and interviews with involved healthcare professionals.
Meadowview's collaboration with local fitness centers provided free trial memberships to attendees as incentives.
The workshops offer hands-on demos of life-saving techniques like CPR, and attendees receive lists of local health resources as they leave.
The note recommends partnering with local pharmacies, clinics and businesses for promotion, funding or in-kind contributions.
Evaluation involves collecting feedback through digital surveys or feedback forms and reviewing the initial objectives against turnout and engagement.
Meadowview has set a follow-up series for the spring, informed by feedback from its fall initiative.
